title: LTS Branch Coordinator and Rollback Simulator
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We lack a lightweight, deterministic coordinator that maps release commits to LTS branches and exercises realistic traffic mixes in a simulator to validate auto-rollback policies before a staged promotion. This leads to last-minute rollbacks and velocity bottlenecks for platform and Dedicated customers.

Goal: Build a small LTS Branch Coordinator service and an accompanying Rollback Simulator that together enable:
- deterministic promotion plans across LTS and non-LTS channels,
- preflight simulations of percent-ramp strategies against historical telemetry,
- automated scoring of rollback likelihood using configurable safety gates (error rate, latency P95, model-quality drift), and
- artifacts (promotion plan + simulation run) attached to the release for audits and postmortems.

Success criteria:
- Coordinator can generate a promotion plan for an LTS branch in < 2s for typical release sizes,
- Simulator can replay 48h of production traffic mix locally and surface a rollback score with 95% reproducibility,
- Reduce unplanned full-rollbacks during LTS promotions by 50% in the first quarter of rollout,
- Promotion artifacts stored in Console and linked in release metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator exposes an API to render promotion plans and accept overrides by Platform SREs
Simulator supports ingesting historical telemetry from BigQuery/Telemetry API and running deterministic runs
Generated promotion plan includes cohort definitions, percent ramps, hold durations, and explicit rollback gates
Console shows promotion artifact link and simulator run summary in release UI
Automated tests for coordinator and simulator included with >=80% unit coverage and integration smoke tests in CI
implementation_plan: Design data model for LTS branch metadata and promotion plan (schema + versioning)
Prototype coordinator: API + small state machine to create promotion graphs and export JSON artifacts
Build rollback simulator: configurable traffic replayer and policy evaluator (pluggable gate rules)
Wire simulator to ingest anonymized telemetry snapshots from BigQuery for deterministic runs
Add UI hooks in Console to attach promotion artifacts and display run summaries
Run alpha with internal services and Dedicated customers willing to test; collect feedback
Iterate on gate thresholds and scoring, add runbook outputs to artifact (why a rollback was triggered)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Simulator fidelity is lower than production; false positives/negatives. Mitigation: begin with a conservative gate threshold and gather ground-truth via shadow runs before enabling any automation.
Risk: Promotion plans add operational overhead. Mitigation: allow one-click auto-generated plan with optional manual edits and clear rollback instructions.
Risk: Data privacy when ingesting telemetry. Mitigation: sanitize PII, use aggregated metrics and pre-approved telemetry snapshots for simulations.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-20: Use a separate lightweight coordinator service instead of extending existing release-controller to keep scope small and enable independent rollout.
Decision 2025-02-25: Simulator will accept BigQuery export snapshots (gzipped parquet) plus an optional live telemetry stream for higher fidelity tests.
Trade-off: Deterministic replay requires controlled randomness sources; we will seed RNGs from snapshot metadata to preserve reproducibility.
Open question: Do we store full simulator traces in Console long-term? For now keep only summaries and links to archived dumps in S3 (30d retention).
